description: Graduate-level real-time and offline rendering: GPU architecture, programmable shading, physically based lighting, shadows and global illumination, ray tracing, modern renderer architectures, temporal techniques and profiling. Students implement shaders and renderers as per-pixel code in the lab, derive the underlying mathematics and finish with a research-style rendering project.
modelledOn: Akenine-Moller, Haines and Hoffman, Real-Time Rendering
Pharr, Jakob and Humphreys, Physically Based Rendering: From Theory to Implementation
Marschner and Shirley, Fundamentals of Computer Graphics
Selected SIGGRAPH course notes on physically based shading and real-time ray tracing
outcomes: Explain how a GPU executes the graphics pipeline and reason about its memory and parallelism limits.
Implement shaders for lighting, texturing and procedural effects, including a physically based BRDF with image-based lighting.
Derive and implement shadowing, ambient occlusion and global illumination approximations and state their errors.
Build a ray or path tracer with an acceleration structure, importance sampling and denoising.
Compare forward, deferred and clustered renderer architectures and choose one for a given workload.
Profile a renderer, identify its bottleneck and apply a justified optimisation, and critique a recent rendering paper.

units.title: GPU architecture and the rendering pipeline
topics: GPU architecture: SIMT execution, warps, occupancy and the memory hierarchy
Pipeline stages: vertex, tessellation, geometry, rasterisation, fragment and compute
Rasterisation: edge functions, barycentric coordinates and perspective-correct interpolation
Depth buffering: early-z, z-fighting and reversed-z with floating-point depth
Homogeneous coordinates and projection matrices: derivation of the perspective matrix

units.title: Programmable shading
topics: Shader languages and stages; uniforms, varyings, textures and buffers
Vertex shader techniques: skeletal skinning, instancing and displacement
Texture sampling: mipmaps, anisotropic filtering and the derivation of aliasing artefacts
Compute shaders: work groups, shared memory and parallel reduction and prefix sum
Procedural shading: Perlin and Worley noise, signed distance functions and ray marching
Tessellation and mesh shaders for geometry amplification and culling

units.title: Physically based shading
topics: Radiometry: radiance, irradiance, the BRDF and the rendering equation
Microfacet models: Cook-Torrance, GGX normal distribution, Smith masking and Schlick Fresnel
Diffuse models and the metallic-roughness material workflow; energy conservation
Image-based lighting: prefiltered environment maps, the split-sum approximation and BRDF lookup table
Linear-space colour, HDR and tone mapping operators (Reinhard, filmic)
Area lights and linearly transformed cosines

units.title: Shadows and global illumination approximations
topics: Shadow mapping: bias, percentage-closer filtering and contact-hardening soft shadows
Cascaded shadow maps for large outdoor scenes and cascade selection
Ambient occlusion: SSAO and horizon-based methods
Indirect lighting approximations: light probes with spherical harmonics, voxel cone tracing and screen-space GI
Reflections: screen-space, planar and probe-based, and their failure cases

units.title: Ray tracing on the GPU
topics: Ray intersection with spheres, triangles and boxes; the Moller-Trumbore test
Bounding volume hierarchies: surface area heuristic build and stackless traversal
Monte Carlo path tracing: importance sampling, next-event estimation and multiple importance sampling
Hardware ray tracing APIs, hybrid raster-plus-ray pipelines and their budgets
Denoising: bilateral and spatiotemporal variance-guided filters
Variance reduction: low-discrepancy sequences, stratification and reservoir resampling

units.title: Renderer architectures
topics: Forward rendering and deferred shading with a G-buffer; memory bandwidth cost
Tiled and clustered light culling with compute shaders
Visibility buffers and material evaluation passes
Transparency: sorted blending, weighted blended and per-pixel linked-list order-independent transparency
GPU-driven rendering: frustum and Hi-Z occlusion culling, level of detail and indirect draw

units.title: Post-processing and temporal techniques
topics: Bloom, depth of field and motion blur from the physical camera model
Temporal anti-aliasing: jittered projection, reprojection, history clamping and ghosting
Spatial anti-aliasing: MSAA, FXAA and SMAA compared
Temporal and spatial upscaling, and checkerboard rendering
Auto-exposure, colour grading and look-up tables

units.title: GPU profiling and optimisation
topics: Measuring a frame: timestamp queries, frame budgets and capture tools
Bandwidth-bound versus ALU-bound work; the roofline model applied to a shader
Occupancy, divergence and register pressure
Mobile and tile-based GPUs: budgets for mid-range phones common across Africa
Draw-call overhead, batching, instancing and pipeline-state sorting

units.title: Research frontiers and project
topics: Reading recent rendering papers: neural radiance fields and Gaussian splatting
Differentiable rendering and inverse problems
Designing a rendering project with a reproducible benchmark
Evaluating image quality: error metrics, perceptual metrics and ground-truth references
Project presentation and peer critique

schedule.title: The pipeline, rasterisation and projection
schedule.exercise: Derive the perspective projection matrix from similar triangles, then explain with a diagram why perspective-correct interpolation needs 1/w and when z-fighting appears.

tasks.title: Rasterise one triangle with edge functions into a 64 by 64 pixel grid and colour each pixel by its barycentric coordinates
Build a perspective projection matrix, project the eight corners of a cube and plot the result for three fields of view
Compare standard and reversed-z depth precision using float32 across a near plane of 0.1 and far plane of 10,000, and chart the resolvable depth step

schedule.title: Shader fundamentals, skinning and sampling
schedule.exercise: Write a vertex transformation for a two-bone skinned limb and derive the mip level from texture coordinate derivatives. Explain aliasing on a checkerboard plane.

tasks.title: Implement linear blend skinning for a two-bone arm in code and render the vertex positions for three bend angles
Generate a mip chain for a checkerboard texture and select the level from screen-space derivatives, comparing against nearest sampling on a receding plane
Implement trilinear and 8-tap anisotropic sampling on a tilted floor, and measure the blur versus aliasing trade-off against a supersampled reference

schedule.title: Compute, procedural shading and mesh amplification
schedule.exercise: Write a parallel reduction and a prefix sum on paper for 16 elements, then build a noise-based terrain pattern and discuss mesh shader culling.

tasks.title: Generate 2D value noise at four octaves and combine them into fractal noise, outputting the result as a greyscale image grid
Emulate a work-group parallel reduction with shared memory in log steps, verify the sum for 1,024 values and count the steps and barriers
Ray march a signed distance field of a smooth-unioned sphere and box with soft shadows, and plot step count per pixel to find the costly regions

schedule.title: Radiometry, BRDFs and the rendering equation
schedule.exercise: Derive the Lambertian BRDF value rho over pi, evaluate the GGX distribution for three roughness values, and show why an energy-conserving material must satisfy the white furnace test.

tasks.title: Plot cosine-weighted irradiance against light angle for a diffuse surface and verify numerically that the albedo over pi BRDF integrates to the albedo
Plot the GGX normal distribution, Smith masking and Schlick Fresnel for roughness 0.1, 0.5 and 0.9 and describe the lobe shape
Render a sphere with Cook-Torrance and Lambert terms, run a white furnace test by Monte Carlo and report the energy lost at high roughness

schedule.title: Image-based lighting, colour and area lights
schedule.exercise: Derive the split-sum approximation for specular image-based lighting, and compare two tone mapping operators on an HDR image with a bright window.

tasks.title: Apply gamma encoding and Reinhard tone mapping to an HDR gradient and compare the output values against clamping
Precompute the BRDF lookup table over view angle and roughness by Monte Carlo sampling with 256 samples per texel and output it as an image
Compare a linearly transformed cosine area light against 4,096-sample Monte Carlo integration for a rectangular light at three roughnesses and report the error

schedule.title: Shadows, occlusion and indirect light
schedule.exercise: Choose cascade split distances for a 1 km view range, explain shadow acne and peter-panning with a diagram, and list what screen-space reflections cannot show.

tasks.title: Render a shadow map for a simple scene and show shadow acne appear and disappear as you change the depth bias
Implement percentage-closer filtering with 16 taps and a variable penumbra width estimated from the blocker search, and compare edge quality
Estimate hemisphere ambient occlusion for a depth buffer, add a one-bounce light probe in spherical harmonics, and compare with a path-traced reference

schedule.title: Ray intersection, BVH and path tracing
schedule.exercise: Derive the Moller-Trumbore test, build a BVH for twelve boxes by hand with the surface area heuristic, and explain the variance difference between uniform and cosine sampling.

tasks.title: Implement ray-sphere and ray-triangle intersection and render a depth image of a small scene with three spheres and one triangle
Build a BVH over 2,000 random triangles with median split and surface area heuristic, and compare traversal counts per ray against brute force
Write a path tracer with next-event estimation and multiple importance sampling for a glossy floor and small light, and plot noise against samples per pixel

schedule.title: Hybrid ray tracing, denoising and sampling
schedule.exercise: Budget a hybrid frame at 60 frames per second on a mid-range GPU, sketch a spatiotemporal denoiser, and compare sampling patterns on a test integral.

tasks.title: Estimate the integral of a 2D function with random, stratified and Halton samples at 64 samples and plot the error of each over 50 runs
Denoise a one-sample-per-pixel noisy render with a joint bilateral filter guided by normals and depth, reporting the error before and after
Build a hybrid frame model where rasterised primary visibility is combined with ray-traced shadows, and chart the ray budget per pixel against frame time

schedule.title: Forward, deferred and clustered rendering
schedule.exercise: For a scene with 500 lights and 1080p resolution, compute the bandwidth of forward, deferred and clustered shading and recommend one with reasons.

tasks.title: Calculate the G-buffer size and per-frame bandwidth for four layouts at 1080p and chart them against a mobile bandwidth budget
Assign 500 point lights to a 16 by 9 by 24 cluster grid on the CPU and report the lights per cluster distribution and the culling accuracy
Implement Hi-Z occlusion culling on a depth pyramid for 10,000 instances and measure the fraction culled against exact visibility

schedule.title: Camera effects and temporal anti-aliasing
schedule.exercise: Derive the circle of confusion for a thin lens, explain history clamping in temporal anti-aliasing, and discuss when upscaling introduces ghosting.

tasks.title: Compute the circle of confusion diameter against object distance for a thin lens at three apertures and plot the in-focus range
Jitter the projection with a Halton sequence, accumulate eight frames with an exponential history and show edge smoothing on a moving square
Add motion-vector reprojection with neighbourhood colour clamping to the accumulator, and measure ghosting and flicker against an unclamped version

schedule.title: Spatial anti-aliasing and exposure
schedule.exercise: Compare MSAA, FXAA and SMAA on a high-contrast scene in terms of cost, quality and what each misses, and derive an auto-exposure rule from average log luminance.

tasks.title: Compute the log-average luminance of an HDR image and set an exposure value that maps middle grey, applying it to three test images
Implement an edge-detecting FXAA-style filter on a rendered line image and compare jagged-edge counts against 4x supersampling
Build a 3D colour grading lookup table from a target look, apply it with trilinear interpolation and measure the colour error on a patch chart

schedule.title: Profiling and optimising a renderer
schedule.exercise: Given a frame time breakdown and shader instruction counts, identify the bottleneck using the roofline model and propose two optimisations with predicted gains.

tasks.title: Plot a frame time breakdown across eight passes from timing data and mark which passes exceed their share of the 16.6 ms budget
Place three shaders on a roofline plot from their arithmetic intensity and decide which are bandwidth bound and which compute bound
Model overdraw and bandwidth for a tile-based mobile GPU, optimise a particle-heavy scene to reach 30 frames per second, and explain each change

schedule.title: Research frontiers and project presentation
schedule.exercise: Present the rendering project with a reproducible benchmark, ground-truth comparison and error metrics, and give a written critique of a peer project.

tasks.title: Compute mean squared error and peak signal-to-noise ratio between a render and a reference image, and report both for three sample counts
Fit the colour of a small sphere to a target image by gradient descent on a differentiable shading function and plot the loss curve
Implement your project technique and a baseline, benchmark both over 10 scenes with confidence intervals, and write up where the technique fails
